A recent market intelligence report states that the cost Apple pays for the iPhone 18 Pro memory will be four times that of last year's model.

TrendForce says Apple will not pass all of the cost on to consumers, and will rely more on service revenue to offset the increase in hardware production costs...

Apple announced major price hikes for most of its products in June this year, saying it had done everything possible to delay the price increases, but was left with no other choice.

At the time, Apple did not raise the price of its existing iPhones, but that situation is expected to change next week. TrendForce points out that memory costs for the new model have increased significantly.

It is expected that Apple will not pass on the full increase in memory costs to the iPhone pricing. The iPhone 18 Pro is currently estimated to cost about $100 more than the iPhone 17 Pro.

The reason is that a significant price hike would cause even the most loyal Apple fans to upgrade their phones less frequently. TrendForce says Apple does not want to sacrifice its continued growth momentum, noting that the weak macroeconomic environment is making consumers more cautious about spending.

The firm expects Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Ultra, to start at $2,299, with the top configuration priced over $3,000.
